Adrian's DeFi Insights 

Автор: Adrian Pape

https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/altcoin-leverage-setting-up-next-flush-adrian-pape-kddke?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BKbvmfONoRPWxl6QCeNAF8A%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=1gA4G_HxCb_Yo1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mtwvalzx~y0-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mtwvalzx-y0
  
Hey, it's Adrian! Last week I put a date on a question. The Treasury was going to step into the long end of the bond market on September 10, and I said that day would tell us whether the liquidity push behind this crypto rally was real. It came. Scott Bessent tripled the buyback instead of doubling it, from $2 billion to $6 billion, and yields went to a three-year high anyway. The 30-year is now at its highest since 2007. Bitcoin is below $77k as I write, down 2% on the day and more than 5% on the week. The more interesting data we got in the derivatives data. For the first time since December 2024, there is more borrowed money sitting on altcoins than on Bitcoin. This led to strong corrections before, so we have to watch out to secure some gains from the last weeks and not give it all back. Let's get into the broader picture and how to set up for the coming week: ⚡ On today's Episode: 📈 Market Update – Brent crude is above $107, the 30-year Treasury hit its highest level since 2007, and the buyback everyone was waiting for made yields worse instead of better. PPI came in hot and the Fed meets September 16 with a 70% chance of a hike priced in. 🔊 Market Pulse – Bitcoin has been turned away four times between $81,265 and $82,283 since August 25 and has now lost $77,000. ETF intake went negative for two straight sessions, spot demand is negative, and the new leverage went into altcoins rather than Bitcoin. Zcash is down 12% today. 🐂 Alpha Insights – I'm still waiting for Bitcoin between $75,700 and $67,000 rather than chasing the golden cross, and my first tranche is now within a thousand dollars of price. I've also started a small SYRUP position as Maple's deposits reach $4.83 billion and trailing revenue hits $22.1 million, with valuation and falling yields still the main risks. Market Update The macro state of the market. Start with the bond market, because that's where the disappointment came from. The Treasury said it would step up its long-end buybacks on September 10. Bessent went further than the announced doubling and tripled the operation, from $2 billion to $6 billion. A buyback is the Treasury buying back its own older bonds. That takes supply out of the market and normally pushes yields down, but only if the size is big enough to matter against how much new debt is being issued alongside it. Six billion wasn't.
